title: Visualization of Full-length Insulin Receptor by Cryo-electron Tomography
content: Insulin receptor (IR) is a receptor tyrosine kinase that plays essential rolls in metabolism, growth and cellular proliferation. The receptor is synthesized as a single polypeptide that is posttranslationally cleaved into two subunits, α and β, which are then cross-linked by multiple disulfide bridges to form a dimer of αβ subunits. Being a constitutive dimer in the absence of ligand makes the IR unique among receptor tyrosine kinases, which are generally single-pass transmembrane proteins. Insulin binding to the α subunit stimulates an intracellular kinase activity in the β chain, which leads to receptor autophosphorylation that creates docking sites for downstream effector and adaptor proteins and initiates intracellular signaling cascades [1].
